subject: zombie
leg: control: Valve's own against the brief
label: zombie, in the place of the game's models/zombie.mdl

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/hgrunt.mdl, models/barney.mdl, models/islave.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked A, B, B, A where the asset was B, D, D, B: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: The outline reads as the brief's scientist: a standing figure about 68 tall, head pushed forward with a tan bulb over it, long arms reaching to the knees, and a slight forward hunch in the side views and in the walk and attack frames. The hunch is mild, but the outline is right in all ten views and no part sticks out or is missing.

M2.reason: Height is 68.4 against the brief's 68, within 0.6%. Measured size is 38.5 x 53.8 x 68.4; the brief gives only a height, so width and length are not held to a number.

M3.reason: Parts the brief asks for, checked down to the small ones: parasite bulb over the head (front, left, back and top views), two arms, two long clawed hands with about four claws each (front and top views), lab coat, trousers, and dark red shoes. The torn coat is shown by painted rips and the chest and back wound with ribs, which is paint on the coat, so it is charged to M4 or M5, not M3. No part is missing and nothing is the wrong count.

M4.reason: Colours match the brief: a white-grey lab coat with red blood on it, a tan-yellow parasite head, dark brown and red claws, and dark red shoes. The colour regions line up with the views, and the blood reads as blood on the coat, not as a different material.

M5.reason: Torn chest and back wounds with ribs and organs, blood smears on the coat and legs, cloth folds, and shoe creases are all there and read at view size. The trousers are a little soft in the back views, which is minor.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 here by the rubric, as M6 is measured on the line-up apart. In the four readings the judges never picked the asset's position as the one not made by Valve (picked A, B, B, A; the asset was at B, D, D, B), so it passed for one of the game's.

M7.reason: Front is the front (open chest and coat facing the front view, the wound on the back). The figure stands upright, and in the walk and attack frames both feet sit on the floor line, so it stands on its origin.

M8.reason: The SMAK check has no errors. 844 triangles is under twice the Half-Life median of 504 (1,008). The underside shows the coat ending open, but that is not visible in play. Nothing floats: the feet stay on the floor line in every walk and attack frame.

C1.reason: Through the walk (0 to 59) and the attack (0 to 35), the head, coat, arms and claws stay on the body and move with it. The arms swing, the claws follow the arms, and the feet stay on the floor line. In the attack the arms raise and sweep without any part coming apart, sinking or floating.
